utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Could I have the appearances please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madame President, Judge Odio Benito, Judge Jan. My name is Mark Harmon. I am representing the Prosecutor's Office today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you, Mr Harmon. MME VIDOVIC: Good afternoon, your Honours. I am Vasvir Vidovic, Minister Counsellor of the Embassy of Bosnia-Herzegovina in The Hague and the BH representative with the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. On May 29th, 1997 the Trial Chamber entered an order to give evidence. It was directed to Mr Mato Tadic, Minister of Justice for the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or his representative from the Ministry of Justice to appear before the Chamber on Friday, 13th June 1997 at 15:00 hours to show cause why the subpoena duces tecum of 30th April 1997 had not been complied with and to be prepared to inform the Trial Chamber what affirmative steps were taken to serve the subpoena duces tecum on Mr Stjepan Ivankovic. Mr Harmon, do you have any matters you wish to present regard this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two matters I would like to raise initially with the Trial Chamber. The first is to report that since the last court order again there has been no production of any documents whatsoever to the Prosecutor's office in response to the subpoena that you issued. My second request is that we go into closed session, because I would like to report some matters to the Trial Chamber in confidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Miss Vidovic, do you have any objection to the Trial Chamber proceeding in closed session? MME VIDOVIC: No, your Honour. I'm in agreement with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MCDONALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we will go into closed session. Before, just to put this matter into some framework, for several months now, I suppose, we have had several hearings regarding subpoenas duces tecum. Bosnia-Herzegovina has not opposed the power or not contended that the Trial Chamber lacks the power to issue a subpoena duces tecum. Instead, we have been attempting to have the various subpoenas served and have the documents requested provided to the Prosecutor. Thus far we have been unsuccessful, but we will continue in closed session and see what steps have been taken, as well as how we should decide how we should proceed from here. So we will stand in recess, I believe, for five minutes and then go on to closed session. (Short break) (In closed session).
